description:
We’re a team of tech and space enthusiasts with skills .We’re excited to build a health monitoring solution for astronauts on long-duration missions.

If you’re creative, collaborative, and excited about space technology, join us!
summary: AstroGalen is an offline-first web app that helps astronauts monitor and understand their own health on long-duration missions. It answers the challenge “Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions” by turning routine readings and two daily physical and mental check-ins into a clear mission-health picture. A mission dashboard tracks vitals such as heart rate, blood pressure, SpO₂ and sleep, plus cabin conditions, and flags readings that leave their healthy range. A Body Explorer links symptoms to spaceflight context, trend charts show changes over time, and an on-device AI assistant gives wellness guidance without internet. It never diagnoses, and it points urgent cases to the crew medical officer. Real NASA data from RadLab (radiation), DONKI (space weather), OSDR (spaceflight studies) and the Human Research Program grounds the guidance. Our prototype uses simulated sensors, clearly labelled DEMO. This matters because on missions to the Moon and Mars, astronauts may be minutes from help and must spot health changes themselves. AstroGalen helps them do it early and act on it.
details: AstroGalen is an offline-first web app that helps astronauts monitor and understand their own health on long missions. A mission dashboard shows 12 live cards: heart rate, blood pressure, sleep, activity, body temperature, SpO₂, radiation dose, and cabin CO₂, pressure and temperature. Readings that leave their healthy range raise a health alert. Each day the astronaut completes two short check-ins, physical and mental, so the app captures how they feel as well as what the sensors show. A Body Explorer links body systems and symptoms to spaceflight context. Insights show trends over time, because a trend matters more than one number. A Medical Test Station adapts to the mission environment (ISS, Moon, Rover or Mars transit). An on-device AI assistant answers questions with no internet. It never diagnoses, and it sends urgent symptoms to the crew medical officer. A medical report can be exported as PDF or JSON.
